title: Grateful Dead Live at Music Hall on 1973-12-01
lineage: Maxell UD90's > Nakamichi CR-5A > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab > R8Brain > CD-Wave > TLH > FLAC 1644 tagged. Transfer by Andrew F.
source: 2 source matrix by dusborne Soundboard (shnid:112205) SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional 11.2 -> FLAC and Audience (shnid:110781) FOB AUD Source: Unknown equipment > MAC taped by Bill Degen. This transfer is 1st Gen cassettes, kindly provided by Tim Friend.

ai_review.summary: Brilliant matrix mix captures an outstanding December 1973 show featuring a smoking Playing in the Band and deep second‑set jams.
ai_review.review: The Dusborne matrix recording is praised as “brilliant” and exceptionally clear, delivering a well‑balanced listening experience. The performance shines with a powerful Playing in the Band (including a vocal coda), a full Uncle John’s Band jam, and an adventurous second set launched by Dark Star/The Other One, while even the later Row Jimmy feels slightly thin in the mix. Overall the show is regarded as one of the best from this period.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both the matrix recording quality and the musical performance, with only a single reviewer noting minor sound thinness.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Matrix blend praised as brilliant and clear; one comment notes occasional thinness during Row Jimmy but no major issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set launched by a Dark Star or The Other One jam, with unusual late placement of Row Jimmy and Greatest Story Ever Told, creating an adventurous and varied flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s riff work is highlighted in the final jam; praised for tight playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is teased by a fan during banter; no specific musical comment.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboards support Garcia’s riffs and add texture to the jams.
